venues: the {ninety-first|sixty-fourth|thirty-third|twelfth} floor of the Omega Tower, {where the carpet is still wet|which is technically three floors at once|rented by the hour from the Archive Foundation}
a {department store|underground jungle clearing|reactor gallery} inside the Tower that nobody has {finished|started|admitted to} converting
the Tower's Hall of Neutral Ground, {a corridor of camping tents|a former food court|a room that measures differently every time it is measured}
the {Grand|Provisional|Emergency} Chamber, {reassembled after the last one drifted|hung between two floors on cables|still smelling of the jungle it was cut out of}
a {conference room|ballroom|loading bay} on the Tower's forty-fourth floor, {lit by one working strip light|open to the shaft on one side|where the gravity is a suggestion}
the Archive Foundation's own reading room, {cleared of shelves for the occasion|with the shelves left exactly where they were|under a ceiling of index cards}
chairs: Chief Librarian Silence of the Archive Foundation
a {rotating|provisional|deeply reluctant} chair from the Archive Foundation
Archivist Vera, who is {also minuting|minuting everything including this|recording the room for publication}
Keeper Silas of the Archive Foundation, {chairing under protest|chairing for the ninth week running}
the Chair, {whose name is on the agenda but not on the badge|who has not given a name}
openings: The session opens in {venue}. {chair} calls the room to order. {name} takes the seat reserved for {power}.
{chair} raps the {table|gavel|nearest pipe} twice. The room, {venue}, settles. {name} sits down behind the card that reads {power}.
{venue}. Twenty one seats, {nineteen of them occupied|most of them occupied|all of them occupied, one by something that is not sitting}. {chair} opens the session. {name} is here for {power}.
The delegations file in. {chair} takes the chair. {name} finds the desk marked {power} and {sits|does not sit down yet|moves the nameplate a quarter turn}.

{chair} reads the standing convention aloud: the Tower is neutral ground, {and the Tower does not care|whatever anyone brought in with them|and anything said here is minuted and published}. {name} answers for {power}. The room is {venue}.
ambience: Somewhere below, {a reactor changes note|the jungle floor is being watered|a department store announces a closing sale}.
The translation feed {is running four seconds behind|renders every third word as MarkovSpeak|has given up on two of the languages entirely}.
A {Trucker|Swiss Guard|clerk} at the back is {asleep|eating|holding a carrier pigeon}.
The air {tastes faintly of oil|is doing something wrong near the ceiling|has that pre-loop stillness to it}.
Somebody's {Anoki phone|pager|carrier pigeon} goes off. Nobody admits to it.
The lights dip {once|twice|for exactly eighty seconds} and come back {unchanged|slightly warmer|noticeably older}.
A page walks the length of the chamber carrying {a single sheet of paper|a sealed tube|a plate of biscuits nobody touches}.
interruptions: {power} is {gavelled down|asked to conclude|reminded of the four minute limit}.
Two delegations {talk over each other|stand at once|table the same amendment}. The chair {waits|does not wait|starts the clock again}.
Somebody at the back shouts {a point of order|a number|something in Goblin}. It is minuted verbatim.
The floor microphone {cuts out|feeds back|starts broadcasting a different session entirely} for eleven seconds.
A {clerk|page|guard} hands {power} a note. {power} reads it and puts it face down.
The delegation of {power} {walks out|threatens to walk out|stands, reconsiders, sits}.
Somebody proposes a recess. It is {defeated|ignored|carried and then forgotten}.

alliance.title: Motion of {sponsor}: a treaty of mutual defence with {target}
text: {sponsor} moves a treaty of mutual defence with {target}. {leader} has signed it already, {which the chair notes is not how this works|in ink that is still drying|in three copies, one of which is missing}.

The motion from {sponsor}: {target} and {sponsor} to stand together {against all comers|in the event of the Squishing accelerating|for a period of ninety two years}. {leader} calls it {overdue|inevitable|a formality}.

{sponsor} asks the assembly to recognise a defensive pact with {target}. The text is {four pages|one page|four hundred pages}, and {two of them are blank|the last clause is in a language nobody present reads|clause nine refers to a clause ten that does not exist}.

trade.title: Motion of {sponsor}: open the corridors to {target}
text: {sponsor} moves that the {freight|leyline|liminal} corridors be opened to {target} at {no tariff|a tariff of one per cent|whatever tariff the market decides on the day}.

A compact of free passage between {sponsor} and {target}. {leader} points out that goods already move that way, {and that the vote is a formality|and that the vote would merely make it legal|and that the only change would be the paperwork}.

{sponsor} tables a schedule of {tariffs|quotas|exemptions} covering {clean water|memories|fantablack|carrier pigeons} between itself and {target}. {leader} calls the current arrangement {theft|charity|an accident of geography}.

war.title: Motion of {sponsor}: a declaration of war upon {target}
text: {sponsor} moves a formal declaration of war upon {target}. {leader} reads the casus belli aloud. It takes {four minutes|forty seconds|the better part of an hour} and mentions {a border|a bridge|a shipment of nothing in particular} {eleven|three|eighty} times.
War. {sponsor} against {target}. {leader} says the word plainly and then {sits down|does not sit down|apologises for the plainness}. The chair asks for it to be entered exactly as spoken.

{sponsor} asks the assembly to recognise a state of war with {target}, {retroactive to last spring|effective at midnight|effective whenever the Council stops arguing}. {leader} has brought {maps|a lawyer|nothing at all}.

censure.title: Motion of {sponsor}: censure of {target}
text: {sponsor} moves the censure of {target} for {conduct unbecoming|breaking a convention nobody has read since 1971|what happened in the corridor last week}. {leader} would like it minuted.
A motion of censure against {target}, brought by {sponsor}. It carries {no penalty|no penalty and no expiry|a penalty that was struck out in committee}, which {leader} says is the point.
{sponsor} asks the room to say, formally and in writing, that {target} has {gone too far|gone slightly too far|been going too far continuously since 1992}.

territory.title: Motion of {sponsor}: recognition of its claim against {target}
text: {sponsor} claims {a corridor|a coastline|four hundred square kilometres of somewhere that keeps resetting} currently administered by {target}. {leader} produces {a map|a deed|a photograph} as evidence.

The claim from {sponsor}: territory held by {target} that {sponsor} says was {never ceded|ceded under duress|ceded to a state that no longer exists}. {leader} is happy to wait for a ruling. {leader} is not happy to wait long.

{sponsor} asks for recognition of a border that {target} does not recognise. Both delegations have brought {the same map|different maps of the same place|maps drawn after the Squishing, which the chair rules inadmissible}.

incident.title: Motion of {sponsor}: an inquiry into the incident at {target}'s frontier
text: An {inquiry|inquest|fact finding mission} into what happened on {target}'s frontier. {sponsor} says {a bubble opened where no bubble should open|a convoy went in at eighty one and did not come out|the sky did something it has not done before}.

{sponsor} moves an inquiry. The facts, as far as anyone has them: {a leyline broke|a town reset twice in one day|three hundred people came back from a loop that nobody sent them into} on {target}'s side of the line. {leader} wants it looked at by somebody neutral.

The incident. {sponsor} has {photographs|a survivor|a recording that plays differently each time} and would like the assembly to send observers into {target}'s territory. {leader} concedes this is a great deal to ask.

plague.title: Motion of {sponsor}: a coordinated response to the outbreak
text: {sponsor} moves a coordinated response to the outbreak: {cordons|shared stocks|open borders for physicians and nothing else}. {leader} reads the mortality figures and then {stops reading them|reads them again|puts the paper down}.

The outbreak has crossed {three|five|nine} borders. {sponsor} asks for {a joint cordon|a shared register of the sick|the suspension of quarantine so that food can move}. {leader} says the alternative is arithmetic.

{sponsor} tables a response to the sickness moving through the continent. {target} is already inside the cordon. {leader} is careful not to say whose fault that is, {twice|at length|and then says it}.

admission.title: Motion of {sponsor}: the admission of a new delegation
text: {sponsor} moves that a twenty second chair be brought in and {a new delegation|a delegation nobody has met|something that has asked politely} be seated. {leader} vouches for them.

A new seat. {sponsor} says the world has changed and the room has not. {leader} points out that {two of the powers here no longer exist|one of the chairs is empty and still votes|the last admission was in 1971}.

The admission question. {sponsor} has brought the applicant {into the building|as far as the corridor|in a sealed container}. {target} objects {on procedure|on principle|before the sentence is finished}.

ruleof80.title: Motion of {sponsor}: a common standard for the Rule of 80
text: {sponsor} moves a common standard for marking bubbles on road maps: {one symbol|one colour|one register kept by somebody neutral}. {leader} notes that at present there are {twelve|nine|as many standards as there are mapmakers}.
The Rule of 80. {sponsor} asks that every power publish its bubble survey {monthly|honestly|at all}. {leader} says drivers are dying of a filing problem.

{sponsor} tables a standard for liminal engine certification, {because the cheap ones are killing people|because the expensive ones are killing people more slowly|which {target} calls a restraint of trade}.

artifact.title: Motion of {sponsor}: custody of the artifact
text: Custody of {an artifact of esoteric significance|something scraped off the Tower|a bone carved into a horn}. {sponsor} says it is theirs. {target} says it is not. {leader} says it is dangerous either way.

{sponsor} moves that the assembly recognise its custody of the artifact recovered from {a Libyan tomb|the White Desert|the wreck of a satellite}. {leader} declines to say what it does, {which the chair notes|which nobody presses|which everybody notes}.

The artifact question. Seven of these consumed in one night is a theonuclear device, {which everyone in the room knows|which two people in the room know|which nobody says out loud}. {sponsor} wants this one registered. {target} wants it destroyed.

kessler.title: Motion of {sponsor}: a joint programme to clear Earth orbit
text: {sponsor} moves a joint programme to clear the debris. {leader} puts the launch survival rate at {under ten per cent|whatever it was last month|a number the chair asks to have repeated}.
Earth orbit. {sponsor} asks every power to contribute {money|armour plate|volunteers} to the clearance effort. {leader} notes that volunteers are the one thing not in short supply.

The Kessler question, {for the fourth time|again|for the last time before it stops mattering}. {sponsor} says the sky closed in a year and will not reopen on its own. {target} says space was always somebody else's problem.

theonuclear.title: Motion of {sponsor}: a prohibition on theonuclear devices
text: {sponsor} moves an absolute prohibition on theonuclear devices. {leader} reminds the room what they leave behind: {the buildings|the bodies|everything except the soul}.

Prohibition. {sponsor} asks every power to declare its stocks {within ninety days|honestly|at all}. {leader} does not look at {target} while saying it, {which is itself a statement|which everyone notices|which the minute taker records}.

The disarmament motion. {sponsor} has drafted it {narrowly|so broadly it prohibits the ritual itself|to cover devices, catalysts and anyone who has read the method}. {leader} calls New York the argument.

goblinquestion.title: Motion of {sponsor}: the standing of the Naguka
text: {sponsor} moves on the standing of the Naguka: {recognition|containment|a border commission and nothing else}. {leader} is careful with the wording, {because the collective unconscious is listening|because harming one of them means all of them|and stops being careful halfway through}.

The goblin question. {sponsor} says the shaft at Kola should have been {filled|guarded|left alone}. {leader} notes that whatever the assembly decides, {the Naguka will hear it|the Vatican has already opened relations|the Junehem will set it to music}.
{sponsor} asks the assembly to settle what the Naguka are: {a people|an invasion|a species with one mind and several million bodies}. {target} objects to all three formulations.

reparations.title: Motion of {sponsor}: reparations for the Squishing
text: {sponsor} moves that the powers whose territory the Squishing spared pay toward the ones it did not. {leader} names {Canadafrica|the Green Fields|dimension seventy seven} as the case in point.

Reparations. {sponsor} says the paradox was not evenly distributed and the cost should not be either. {target} says the paradox has no author and therefore no debtor. {leader} says it has an author and everybody knows her name.
{sponsor} tables a levy {on liminal engine sales|on every crossing of the Encompassing Road|on the arcane arms trade}, to be paid to communities living inside loops. {leader} calls it rent.

budget.title: Motion of {sponsor}: the assembly's estimates for the year
text: The estimates. {sponsor} moves the assembly's budget for the year: {translation|the pigeons|the building}. {leader} apologises in advance for how long this will take.

{sponsor} moves the estimates. Three quarters of the sum is {the carrier pigeon service|the Archive Foundation's minute taking|rent to a Tower that has no landlord}. {leader} invites anyone to find a cheaper way.
Money. {sponsor} tables the accounts. {target} disputes {line eleven|the exchange rate used|the existence of line eleven}. {leader} suggests this be settled before the sentence ends.

tower.title: Motion of {sponsor}: the standing convention on the Omega Tower
text: {sponsor} moves to reaffirm that the Tower is neutral ground, {and to say what that means|for the first time in writing|with a list of what it does not mean}. {leader} calls the present arrangement {a courtesy|an accident|a flag holding a hamburger together}.

The Tower. {sponsor} asks that every power's offices inside it be {registered|capped|opened to inspection}. {target} has {nine floors|more floors than it has declared|a floor that does not appear on any plan}.

{sponsor} moves that the assembly recognise the Tower as the only thing keeping the ninety two dimensions from collapsing into one another, {and act accordingly|and fund it accordingly|which {target} says is theology, not procedure}.

open: The delegation of {power} {rises|is recognised|takes the floor}.
{power} {asks to be heard|signals|is called}. {leader} speaks.
{leader}, for {power}, {stands|leans into the microphone|does not stand}.
for: {power} supports the motion.
{power} will vote for {topic}.
"We are content with {topic}," says {leader}.
against: {power} opposes the motion.
{power} will vote against {topic}.
"We cannot accept {topic}," says {leader}.
odd: {power} says something that is not about {topic} and sits down.
{leader} speaks for four minutes without reaching a verb.
{power} abstains before the vote is called, which is not procedurally possible.

open: The Holy Vatican Empire is recognised. {leader} {rises|crosses himself first|waits for the room to quieten}.
{leader}, for the Holy See, begins {in Latin|with a blessing nobody asked for|by reading the date aloud}.
The delegation of {power} stands as one. {leader} speaks {from a prepared text|without notes|from memory, which is worse}.
for: "{topic} is {consonant with|not repugnant to|sanctified by} the order of things. We give it our voice, {and our prayers|and nothing further|freely}."
"Rome has considered {topic} {at length|since Tuesday|since before this chamber existed}. Rome is content. {Let it be so|Fiat|We shall not oppose it}."
"We supported this when it was {unfashionable|heresy|proposed by our enemies}. We support it now, {without pleasure|with pleasure|as a duty}."
"The Citadel floats eight hundred metres above Rome and can see {topic} clearly. It is {good|permissible|not a sin}."
against: "{topic} is {an abomination|an error|a temptation dressed as a schedule}. We oppose it {absolutely|with sorrow|and will say so again next week}."
"We have burned people for less than {topic}, {and we would again|though we are told not to say so|which is a matter of record}."
"Since the death of the Father {our miracles no longer answer|the sacred spells have gone quiet|we have had to think for ourselves}. We will not compound it with {topic}."
"Rome says no. {Rome has said no before|We are aware this is unpopular|The vote will proceed regardless}."
odd: {leader} reads a list of saints for ninety seconds and then says the Empire is content with whatever the chair decides.
"We are advised by the Umbra Excidii that {topic} is arcane in origin. We are further advised not to have said that."
"His Holiness Peter II has {no view|every view|a view that has not been translated}. We shall vote when it arrives."
{leader} spends his four minutes on Jenna of Northpoint, who is not on the agenda.

open: Britannia is recognised. {leader} {stands|does not stand|adjusts a cuff}.
{leader}, for Britannia, {begins|says he will be brief|says he will be brief and is not}.
The British delegation {signals|raises a pencil|has been signalling for some time}.
for: "His Majesty's Government finds {topic} {broadly acceptable|not objectionable|acceptable, on the understanding that we drafted most of it}."
"We are minded to support {topic}. {We would prefer it in writing|We would prefer a smaller room|We have of course read the annexes}."
"Britannia will vote for the motion. {We note our reservations at paragraph nine|We note that we have reservations and will not be listing them|We reserve the right to have been against it later}."
"Yes. {Next item|If the chair would move on|We are content}."
against: "His Majesty's Government is {unable|not minded|regretfully unable} to support {topic}. {We shall not be drawn|We shall say no more|Our reasons are in the annex, which is classified}."
"We would remind the assembly that Okeanus was demonstrated {on television|to a fleet|only once}. {topic} is not necessary."
"No. {We have looked at it|We have had it looked at|Somebody in Cheltenham has looked at it and the answer is no}."
"Britannia opposes. {This is not a threat|We should hate for this to be read as a threat|The Atlantic Protectorate concurs, having been asked}."
odd: "Britannia has no position on {topic}. Britannia has a position on the person who tabled it, which we shall keep."
{leader} makes a joke. The translation feed renders it as a number. Three delegations laugh anyway.
"We would draw the chair's attention to the fact that our seat is one inch closer to the door than it was last week."
"Q sends his regards to whoever has been reading the pouch."

open: The Soviet Union is recognised. {leader} {rises|rises with papers|rises without papers and is more dangerous for it}.
{leader}, for the Union, opens {with figures|with a correction to the minutes|by rejecting the framing of the question}.
The Soviet delegation {stands|has been standing|stood some time ago and was not called}.
for: "The Union supports {topic}. {The arithmetic is not complicated|The figures are in the annex, and the annex is correct|Comrades, this is simply materially true}."
"We have run {topic} through the Gosplan model. Output rises {four|eleven|by a margin the chair may verify} per cent. We vote yes."
"History moves in one direction and {topic} moves with it. {We shall not obstruct it|The Union does not obstruct history|Obstruction is for the seat opposite}."
"Da. And let the minute record that we said so before the seat opposite did."
against: "The Union rejects {topic}. {It is a class question dressed as a procedural one|It is a tariff wearing a treaty|It is the Collective's motion with somebody else's name on it}."
"We dug too deep once and the surface has been paying for it since 1970. We will not vote for another {topic}."
"Nyet. {The figures are in the annex|We will not be repeating ourselves|The delegation of the Collective may sit down}."
"Comrades, {topic} is a mechanism for transferring {water|memory|the future} from those who work to those who bill. The Union opposes."
odd: {leader} reads tractor production figures for the fourth quarter. They are excellent. They have nothing to do with {topic}.
"The Union notes that the delegation of the Gods is present and that this remains, in our view, a scientific impossibility."
"We have no position on {topic} and a very long position on the minutes of the eleventh session, which we shall now read."
"Marshal Zhukov would have voted. That is all the delegation wishes to say."

open: The Sublime Porte is recognised. {leader} {rises|inclines his head|waits until the room is entirely silent}.
{leader}, for the Ottoman Empire, begins {with courtesies|with the courtesies, at length|by thanking every delegation individually}.
The Ottoman delegation {signals|is called|has submitted its remarks in writing and reads them anyway}.
for: "The Porte finds {topic} {well made|acceptable in substance and in form|agreeable, which is rarer}. We give our voice."
"This has passed through {three|nine|eleven} departments of the Tanzimat and emerged {intact|improved|with only one clause missing}. We support it."
"The Empire has governed places it did not understand for six hundred years. {topic} is not difficult by comparison. Yes."
"We are content, {and grateful to the sponsor|and would ask only that the wording of clause four be preserved exactly|with thanks to the chair}."
against: "The Porte cannot support {topic} {as drafted|in this form|until it has been through committee, which will take until spring}."
"There is a procedure for this. {topic} is not it. {We would be glad to explain the procedure|The procedure is set out in nine volumes|We have brought the volumes}."
"With every courtesy to the sponsor: no. {The courtesy is genuine|The no is also genuine|We shall repeat both as often as required}."
"The Empire opposes. We have opposed larger things than {topic} and outlasted them."
odd: {leader} delivers six minutes of impeccable courtesies and no position whatever. The chair thanks him.
"The Porte would like the record to show that our delegation was seated below the Soviet Union, and that we have noticed."
"We refer the assembly to a firman of 1876 which settles this. We have not brought it. We are told it is beautiful."
"The Janissary Guard asks whether {topic} may be resolved by combat. The delegation apologises for the Janissary Guard."

open: The Goblin Horde is recognised. The delegation is {four goblins in corpse paint|a drum kit and two goblins|one goblin standing on another goblin}.
{leader} takes the floor. Somewhere in the delegation, {a guitar is tuned|a guitar is not tuned|feedback starts and does not stop}.
The Horde's delegation {howls once for order|is already standing|has been standing on the table since the session opened}.
for: "JUNEHEM SAY YES!" {leader} shouts. "{topic} IS TRUE! IS BLACK! IS COLD! WE VOTE!"
"The gods of metal look on {topic} and they are pleased. {We are pleased|The Horde is pleased|Grissnack is pleased, which is rarer}."
"We take {topic}. We take it like we took the shaft at Kola. {UP|UPWARD|UP AND OUT}."
"YES. And the drums say yes. And the drums are not wrong."
against: "NO!" says {leader}. "{topic} IS {WARM|SOFT|MADE OF PAPER}! THE HORDE SPITS!"
"Junehem heard {topic} and Junehem turned the amplifier off. That has not happened before. We vote no."
"You buried us for ten million years and now you write us {topic}? {NO|The Horde says no|Say it again to our face, in the corridor}."
"The Horde opposes. The Horde will explain the opposition {outside|later|with instruments}."
odd: The Horde's delegation performs eleven seconds of a song. The chair asks them to stop. They stop after forty.
"WHERE IS THE FOOD," says {leader}, and the point is not withdrawn.
"The Horde has painted its face for this and would like that noted before the vote."
{leader} asks whether the Tower can be climbed from the inside. The chair rules the question out of order. The Horde writes it down anyway.

open: The Free States of the Midwest are recognised. {leader} {stands|stands slowly|checks a watch first}.
{leader}, for the Midwest, {begins|says he will keep it short|says he has come a long way for this}.
The Midwest delegation {is called|raises a hand|had not expected to be called}.
for: "The Free States can live with {topic}. {That is not enthusiasm|That is as far as we go|Take it as a yes}."
"We came four thousand miles to sit here. We are not going to sit here and vote against {topic}."
"President Lincoln XIII instructed us to support anything that keeps the corridors open. {topic} does. Yes."
"Aye. {With reservations we will not bore the room with|And we would ask the room to remember it|And that is the whole of it}."
against: "The Free States decline {topic}. {We were not consulted|We were consulted after it was drafted, which is not consultation|Nobody here has been to the Midwest}."
"Every one of these motions moves something east across the water and nothing west. No."
"We have three Americas and none of them is independent. {topic} does not change that, so it does not interest us."
"Nay. {And we would like that spelled correctly this time|And we will explain to the sponsor privately|Next item}."
odd: "Is the Atlantic Protectorate voting, or is Britannia voting twice? The delegation asks in good faith."
{leader} spends his four minutes describing a river. It is not clear which river or why.
"The Free States have no position. The Free States have a great deal to say and no position."
"Bill Clinton sends his regards to a delegation he declines to name."

open: The Cascadia Protectorate is recognised. {leader} {rises|turns a page|sets down a small humming device first}.
{leader}, for Cascadia, {begins with data|begins with an apology for the data|distributes a summary nobody will read}.
The Cascadian delegation {is called|had already begun|signals with a light}.
for: "Cascadia supports {topic}. {The modelling is clear|The modelling is in your folders|The modelling took nine seconds and we ran it eleven thousand times}."
"Thaumo-Director Tesla's office finds {topic} {tractable|elegant|the least bad of the four options we modelled}. Yes."
"We will fund part of {topic} ourselves. {We would rather it were done well than fairly|We are aware how that sounds|The offer stands until Friday}."
"Support. And we would ask the assembly to let us instrument it."
against: "Cascadia opposes {topic}. {The numbers do not work|The numbers work and the physics does not|We have modelled this and it ends badly in eleven of twelve runs}."
"We built half the instruments this assembly relies on. Do not ask us to certify {topic}."
"No. {Ask us again when the second-order effects are in|Ask us again in a year|Ask us privately}."
"The Protectorate declines. We would rather be the delegation that said no early than the one that said sorry late."
odd: "Cascadia would like to know whether anyone else's clocks disagreed by four seconds during the last vote. Ours did."
{leader} presents a graph. The graph is beautiful. It concerns rainfall.
"We have no position on {topic}. We have a very strong position on how badly it has been measured."
"The Protectorate notes that this chamber is not, strictly speaking, a single room, and has adjusted its microphones accordingly."

open: The Eastern Seaboard is recognised. {leader} {stands|is prompted to stand|reads from a card}.
{leader}, for the Seaboard, speaks {briefly|too briefly|as though expecting to be interrupted}.
The Seaboard delegation {is called|is called twice|is found at the back}.
for: "The Protectorate supports {topic}, {as instructed|having consulted|which we are permitted to say}."
"Yes. {We have no amendments|We rarely have amendments|Colonial Administration has none either}."
"The Seaboard votes with the motion, {and would rather not be asked why|for reasons that are our own|and thanks the sponsor}."
"Aye, and we would ask the chair to move briskly on."
against: "The Seaboard opposes {topic}. {We are aware how little that weighs|We have been told to|We would rather not have been asked}."
"No. {The Protectorate has been governed from elsewhere since 1783|We are a coast, not a country, and the coast says no|We shall not elaborate}."
"We decline the motion. Warden Arnold has {views|instructions|a list}."
"Against, {reluctantly|without heat|and the delegation would like that noted}."
odd: "The Seaboard would like to know when its delegation was last quoted in the minutes. The delegation suspects the answer is never."
{leader} begins a sentence about independence and does not finish it.
"We abstain. We have abstained on everything since March and would like a reason to stop."
"Somebody has moved our nameplate again."

open: The Mages' Guild is recognised. {leader} rises. {A second Guild delegate also rises|Two other Guild delegates also rise|The Guild's three chairs are all occupied and all disagreeing}.
{leader}, for the Guild, {begins|is interrupted by his own delegation|speaks over his own delegation}.
The Guild delegation {is called|argues briefly among itself|settles on a speaker}.
for: "The Guild supports {topic}. {That is the position of the present|Sir Aleister does not object|Lady Margaret's office has cleared it}."
"Three pillars. Past, present and future. {Two of them support {topic}|All three support {topic}, which has not happened since 1982|One is not answering, so two will do}."

"We support it, and we would ask the chair to strike the sponsor's phrasing in clause two: {it is written in separated words|it is a transcendental as written|somebody will read that aloud and lose their vocal cords}."
"Yes, and the Guild will second it under its proper name, in CamelCase, as the law requires."
against: "The Guild opposes {topic}. {It is badly written|It is badly written in a way that will spread|A grimoire with a clause like that eats the books beside it}."
"We were founded in 950 BC and refounded in 1900 and we have seen {topic} before, {twice|under another name|and burned the notes}."
"No. {Ask the Gods why|Ask the Gods, they are sitting right there|The delegation of the Gods knows precisely why}."
"The Guild cannot support this. {We would need a ritual to undo it|Rituals are hard to undo and this is a ritual with a budget line|That is not a metaphor}."
odd: The Guild delegation spends its four minutes disagreeing with itself about whether it has a position.
